voice-message.context: A speech bubble holding three vertical bars of different heights, like an audio waveform. Used for recorded voice notes in chat apps.

video-message.context: A speech bubble with a play triangle inside. Used for short recorded video clips sent in chat or messaging apps.

photo-message.context: A speech bubble with a small picture of a mountain and a sun inside. Used for image attachments and picture messages in chat.

shared-contact.context: A speech bubble with a head-and-shoulders silhouette inside. Used for contact cards shared in a conversation.

group-chat.context: A speech bubble with three heads in a row inside it. Used for group conversations, team channels and community chats.

direct-message.context: A speech bubble with a small paper plane inside. Used for private direct messages and inbox threads.

quick-reply.context: A speech bubble with a lightning bolt inside. Used for fast canned answers, suggested replies and auto responses.

emoji-reaction.context: A speech bubble with a smiley face overlapping its lower corner. Used to react to a message with an emoji.

chatbot.context: A speech bubble with a robot face, antenna and square eyes. Used for automated assistants and support bots.

ai-chat.context: A speech bubble with a four-point sparkle inside. Used for AI assistants, generated replies and smart chat features.

shout-bubble.context: A jagged starburst speech balloon with a pointed tail. Used for shouting, loud exclamations and comic-style emphasis.

whisper-bubble.context: A round speech balloon drawn with a dashed outline and a small tail. Used for whispers, quiet or private remarks.

forwarded-message.context: A speech bubble with a double right-pointing chevron inside. Used to mark a message that was passed on from another conversation.

text-emoticon.context: A speech bubble holding a colon and a bracket that form a sideways smile. Used for text emoticons, typed smileys and casual chat.

meme-image.context: A picture frame with a thick text bar across the top and bottom and a simple smiling face between them. Used for memes and captioned images.

audio-room.context: Four small avatar heads arranged around a central microphone. Used for live audio rooms and social voice spaces.

live-reactions.context: Three outlined hearts floating upward in a staggered trail. Used for live stream reactions and audience love.

link-in-bio.context: A phone screen with a round avatar at the top and three stacked link buttons below. Used for creator profile link pages.

profile-banner.context: A wide cover rectangle with a round avatar overlapping its bottom edge. Used for profile headers on social and community pages.

q-and-a.context: A speech bubble with a question mark and a round bubble with a check mark overlapping its corner. Used for question and answer features and help forums.

love-letter.context: A closed envelope with a heart sealing the point of its flap. Used for romantic mail, Valentine cards and messages of affection.

red-envelope.context: A tall narrow envelope with a band near the top and a round emblem in the centre. Used for gifts of money at festivals and celebrations.

stamped-envelope.context: An envelope front with a small stamp in the top-right corner and address lines. Used for postal mail and sending letters.

registered-mail.context: An envelope with a large letter R on its front. Used for certified, tracked or recorded postal delivery.

return-to-sender.context: An envelope with a curved U-turn arrow looping back over it. Used for undeliverable or returned mail.

email-signature.context: An envelope with a handwritten signature scribble along its lower half. Used for email sign-offs and signed messages.

out-of-office.context: An envelope with a small palm tree standing beside it. Used for away messages and automatic vacation replies.

mailing-list.context: An envelope on the left with three bulleted list lines beside it. Used for subscriber lists and email distribution groups.

junk-mail.context: A tilted envelope drooping over the rim of a small wastebasket. Used for spam, unwanted flyers and deleting mail.

cluster-mailbox.context: A pedestal cabinet with a grid of small mail doors standing on a short post. Used for shared neighbourhood or apartment mailboxes.

stamp-coil.context: A roll of postage stamps with a strip of stamps unwinding from it. Used for postal supplies and stamp shopping.

pen-pal.context: An envelope in front of a small globe. Used for international correspondence and letters sent abroad.

delivery-door-tag.context: A door hanger card with a round hole at the top and a small parcel symbol below. Used for missed delivery notices left at the door.

customs-form.context: A form sheet with a globe at the top and rows of checkboxes below. Used for customs declarations on international parcels.

signature-pad.context: A handheld tablet with a stylus signing a squiggle on its screen. Used for proof of delivery signatures and sign-here devices.

parcel-tracking.context: A parcel box with a map pin above it and dots leading away as a route. Used for package tracking and delivery status.

mail-bicycle.context: A bicycle with a large front basket holding an envelope. Used for courier bikes and local letter delivery.

invitation-card.context: An envelope with a card sticking out that carries a ribbon bow. Used for party, wedding and event invitations.

rsvp-card.context: A small reply card with a ticked box and a crossed box, each beside a line. Used for attendance responses to events.

guestbook.context: An open book with a pen lying across its pages. Used for visitor books and sign-in registers.

payphone.context: A wall-mounted box phone with a handset on its side, a coin slot and a keypad. Used for public pay telephones.

candlestick-phone.context: An upright stick telephone with a flat mouthpiece on top and a separate earpiece hanging on a hook. Used for antique telephone themes.

flip-phone.context: A clamshell mobile phone opened, with a small screen on the upper half and a keypad on the lower half. Used for retro mobile themes.

feature-phone.context: A candy-bar mobile phone with a small screen above a grid of number keys. Used for basic keypad phones.

brick-phone.context: A large brick-shaped early mobile phone with a stubby antenna. Used for retro and early cellular themes.

satellite-phone.context: A chunky rugged handset with a thick tilted antenna and a small screen. Used for remote and off-grid communication.

foldable-phone.context: A book-style folding smartphone shown half open with a hinge down the middle. Used for foldable and dual-screen devices.

wall-phone.context: A wall-mounted phone with a dial and a handset on its side with a long coiled cord. Used for landline and retro home phone themes.

bluetooth-earpiece.context: A single ear-hook earpiece with a capsule body and a short boom microphone. Used for hands-free wireless calling.

rotary-dial.context: A round dial disc with a ring of finger holes and a curved finger stop. Used for rotary telephone themes.

phone-card.context: A prepaid card with a chip on the left and a small telephone handset on the right. Used for calling cards and phone credit.

caller-id.context: A telephone handset next to a small id card with a person silhouette. Used for caller identification on incoming calls.

call-transfer.context: A telephone handset with two opposing horizontal arrows above it. Used for transferring a call to another person or line.

conference-call.context: A telephone handset with three small head figures above it. Used for multi-party audio calls.

call-merge.context: Two lines converging into one arrow above a telephone handset. Used for combining separate calls into one.

hang-up.context: A telephone handset lying horizontally with both ends pointing down. Used for ending or declining a call.

call-log.context: A telephone handset beside three short horizontal list lines. Used for call history and recent calls.

phone-speed-dial.context: A telephone handset with a small lightning bolt beside it. Used for quick dial and favorite numbers.

call-on-hold.context: A telephone handset with two vertical pause bars beside it. Used when a call is paused or placed on hold.

call-waiting.context: A telephone handset with three dots in a row beside it. Used for a second incoming call or a call in a queue.

call-recording.context: A telephone handset with a filled record dot inside a ring. Used for recorded calls and call monitoring.

emergency-call.context: A telephone handset with a bold medical cross beside it. Used for urgent help lines and emergency services.

international-call.context: A telephone handset beside a small globe. Used for overseas and long-distance calls.

robocall.context: A telephone handset beside a simple robot head with an antenna. Used for automated and recorded-message calls.

phone-tree.context: A small telephone handset at the top with lines branching down to three boxes. Used for automated call menus and routing.

phone-number.context: A telephone handset above a short row of dots and a dash standing for digits. Used for displaying or entering a contact number.

field-telephone.context: A boxy portable telephone with a hand crank on its side and a handset on top. Used for military and vintage field communication themes.

captioned-telephone.context: A desk phone with a large screen showing text lines beside the handset. Used for live call captions for people who are hard of hearing.

tty-device.context: A keyboard unit with a small text display and a telephone handset resting on top. Used for text telephone services for deaf users.

video-phone.context: A desk phone with a small screen showing a smiling face above a keypad. Used for face-to-face desk video calls.

acoustic-coupler.context: A modem box with two round rubber cups holding a telephone handset on top. Used for retro dial-up and early computer networking themes.

video-conference.context: A monitor on a stand divided into a two by two grid with a head in each cell. Used for online team video meetings.

webinar.context: A screen showing a presenter at the top and a row of small audience heads below. Used for online seminars and live presentations.

breakout-rooms.context: A large rectangle split into four rooms with openings, each holding a small person dot. Used for splitting a meeting into small groups.
